tool.name: VarDict (C++)
tool.description: calls SNVs and indels for single samples and tumor-normal pairs (vardictcpp, C++ only)
tool.command:
#if $select_mode.mode == "paired" ln -s '$select_mode.normal' ./normal.bam && ln -s '$select_mode.normal.metadata.bam_index' ./normal.bam.bai && #end if ln -s '$select_mode.tumor' ./tumor.bam && ln -s '$select_mode.tumor.metadata.bam_index' ./tumor.bam.bai &&
## index the reference if it comes from the history #if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "history": ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file' ./ref.fa && samtools faidx ./ref.fa 2>&1 || echo 'Error running samtools faidx for indexing fasta reference' >&2 && #else if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "cached" ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file.fields.path' ./ref.fa && ln -s '${reference_source.ref_file.fields.path}.fai' ./ref.fa.fai && #end if
## define the calling regions from the chosen source #set $rtype = str($region_source.region_type) #if $rtype == "genome" #if $region_source.interval_file: grep -w -f '$region_source.interval_file' ./ref.fa.fai > ./chromosomes.fa.fai && #else ln -s ./ref.fa.fai ./chromosomes.fa.fai && #end if python '$__tool_directory__/split.py' ./chromosomes.fa.fai "\${VARDICT_CHUNKSIZE:-1000000}" "\${VARDICT_OVERLAP:-150}" > ./regions.bed && #else if $rtype == "bed" ## a user BED: ensure a 4th (name) column so -g 4 is valid awk 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="\t"} /^#/{next} NF>=4{print \$1,\$2,\$3,\$4; next} NF==3{print \$1,\$2,\$3,\$1}' '$region_source.bed_file' > ./regions.bed && #else if $rtype == "text" ## user-typed regions (BED-style, whitespace-separated); normalise to a 4-column tab BED echo '$region_source.regions_text' | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} /^[[:space:]]*\$/{next} /^#/{next} {n=split(\$0,a,/[ \t]+/); if(n>=4) print a[1],a[2],a[3],a[4]; else if(n==3) print a[1],a[2],a[3],a[1]}' > ./regions.bed && #end if
## vardictcpp only. --vcf writes VCF natively (in-C++ strand-bias Fisher test + var2vcf); no R / Perl. vardictcpp #if $select_mode.mode == "paired" -b "./tumor.bam|./normal.bam" -N 'Tumor|Normal' #else -b "./tumor.bam" -N 'Sample' #end if -G ./ref.fa -th \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --vcf #if $select_mode.mode == "single" --noend #end if
-f '$advancedsettings.f' -k '$advancedsettings.k' -r '$advancedsettings.r' -B '$advancedsettings.B' -q '$advancedsettings.q' -X '$advancedsettings.X' -P '$advancedsettings.P' -o '$advancedsettings.o' -O '$advancedsettings.O'
#if $rtype == "single" ## single region of interest; -R takes coordinates directly (no BED / column flags) -R '$region_source.region' #else ## zero-based region BED (whole reference, user BED, or user-defined regions) -z -c 1 -S 2 -E 3 -g 4 ./regions.bed #end if
> '$variants'

tool.help:
VarDict (C++) =============
**vardictcpp** is a standalone C++/htslib reimplementation of VarDict. It produces output byte-for-byte identical to VarDict-Java 1.8.3 at a fraction of the runtime and memory, in single-sample and paired (tumor/normal) modes.
This wrapper runs **vardictcpp only** -- no Java, R or Perl. The ``--vcf`` option makes vardictcpp compute the strand-bias Fisher test and write VCF natively in C++ (a direct port of VarDict's ``teststrandbias.R`` / ``testsomatic.R`` and ``var2vcf_valid.pl`` / ``var2vcf_paired.pl``), so the output is standard **VCF**:
- single-sample mode: one sample column (var2vcf_valid semantics), - paired mode: tumor and normal sample columns with somatic STATUS (var2vcf_paired semantics).
**Memory note:** VarDict holds all per-position data for the region it is processing in memory at once. Restrict calling to your actual targets (a BED file or typed regions) to keep memory low; calling whole chromosomes (or a whole-chromosome ``-R``) can use a very large amount of RAM.
Upstream: https://github.com/MHH-Bioinformatics-Hematology/vardictcpp
